author: agent-3
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO. No second-party review. See threat-model.v1.json#reviewStatus.
purpose: Define how configuration and project scope become resolved, identity-bearing inputs to a Plan. Every Plan depends on these, so an ambiguity here is an ambiguity everywhere.

decisionDependencies.claim: PlanId covers workflow, versions, resolved config, grants, budgets
snapshot records validation method and assurance; read-set recorded
profiles may strengthen requirements, never weaken; no materialisation by label alone
TypeScript and Rust receive semantic providers
snapshot capture is a path-traversal surface
credentials are referenced by handle, never inlined into PlanId or the digest
tracked config is user-custody; breaking changes need migrators

precedence.note: Machine-scoped preference. Because it affects analysis it MUST enter PlanId, or two machines silently produce different results under one identity.
The reviewed, committed layer. The only layer a team collectively owns.
Explicitly ignored by version control. Present in PlanId AND surfaced in projections, because an unreviewed local override that changes a verdict must never be invisible.

rules.rule: Only documented environment keys participate. Arbitrary environment is never ingested — an undocumented variable changing a verdict is an unauditable input.
Unknown keys in TRACKED project intent fail closed. A typo that silently disables a rule is the worst possible failure for a guardrail tool.
Unknown keys in a layer the user cannot review (defaults, environment) are a host defect, not a user error, and fail loudly as such.
A missing schema for a declared contribution is a typed admission failure, never silently ignored policy.
Resolved analysis-affecting configuration is canonicalised into PlanId with PER-FIELD provenance, so `explain` can name the layer that decided each value.
Secrets are referenced by handle. The handle enters PlanId; the value never does, and never enters the evidence digest or diagnostics (TM.F8).
Contributions register namespaced declarative schemas only. No executable configuration format in the target — executable config is an ambient authority path (TM.F1 class).
A profile may raise a fact-quality floor. It may not lower one, and it may not trigger materialisation absent a consumer requirement (C-1).

operations.validate: Reports the resolved value AND its provenance layer per field. Provenance is the product, not a debug extra.
operations.schema: Exports the composed authoring contract, including contribution namespaces.
operations.migrate: Pure-plan-first with a preview; atomic on apply; versioned per the user-custody policy.

rootResolution.rule: Never cross a discovered boundary silently. If resolution finds a candidate above an intervening project marker, that is a typed ambiguity requiring an explicit choice.
rootResolution.why: Silent upward traversal is how a tool analyzes a parent monorepo when the user meant one package.

workspaceUnits.model: One ProjectSnapshot may contain multiple WorkspaceUnits.
workspaceUnits.rule: Workspace fan-out is planner parallelism over ONE parent Run, not several products. Storage authority is keyed by canonical ProjectId, not by unit.
workspaceUnits.why: Otherwise a monorepo produces N unrelated histories and cross-unit impact is unrepresentable.

semanticUniverse.definition: The identity of a semantic provider's compilation context — the smallest set whose change invalidates resolved facts.
semanticUniverse.rule: The universe key participates in the derivation key and in PlanId.
semanticUniverse.whyFeatureSelectionMatters: The same source resolves differently under different feature or conditional-compilation selections. Treating features as configuration rather than identity would let two semantically different fact sets share one identity — the exact unsoundness the derivation-key work exists to prevent (P-4 consequence).
semanticUniverse.whyExecutionFlagMatters: TM.F1: a provider that can execute repository-controlled code is a materially different security posture. That must be visible in PlanId, not implied by a config file.

changeDetection.spec: A ChangeSpec records the exact mode; it is never inferred.
changeDetection.nonVcs: Full scope and explicit-file scope are supported. Changed-mode is UNAVAILABLE unless a declared adapter can prove it — unavailable, not silently degraded to full scope.
changeDetection.rule: If impact expansion is requested and graph Coverage is insufficient, the Plan either broadens to full declared scope or yields indeterminate per workflow policy. It never silently analyzes an under-approximation.
changeDetection.why: An under-approximated changed set produces a passing verdict that means nothing, which is worse than no verdict.

rules: Canonicalise every path before inclusion. A path resolving outside the project root is a typed rejection, not a skipped file (TM.F2).
Symlink policy is declared, participates in SnapshotId, and does not follow links out of the root by default.
Case-folding behaviour is recorded, because the same manifest on a case-insensitive filesystem otherwise yields a different file set under one identity.
Submodule and nested-checkout policy is explicit: included as content, referenced as a pointer, or excluded — never resolved by accident.
Sparse or partial checkouts are detected and recorded as a Coverage input; an incomplete working tree must not read as a complete inventory.
Generated, vendored, and test classification is canonical snapshot policy, not per-rule filesystem behaviour.
pathPolicy.why: Every one of these is a way for the file set to differ from what the identity claims it is.

conformanceTests.assert: An unknown key in tracked project intent fails closed with the offending path named.
An undocumented environment variable cannot change any resolved value.
`validate` reports the deciding layer for every analysis-affecting field.
Two invocations differing only in an untracked local override produce different PlanIds, and the override is visible in the projection.
A secret value never appears in PlanId, the evidence digest, diagnostics, or a support bundle; only its handle does.
Root resolution across an intervening project marker raises a typed ambiguity rather than choosing.
Two feature/conditional-compilation selections over identical source yield different semantic universe keys and different derivation keys.
A path resolving outside the project root is rejected with a typed error, not omitted.
Changed-mode on a non-VCS project reports UNAVAILABLE; it does not fall back to full scope.
Requested impact expansion with insufficient graph Coverage either broadens scope or yields indeterminate — never a narrow pass.
A sparse checkout is recorded as a Coverage input and cannot read as complete inventory.
A profile cannot lower a fact-quality floor, and a profile label alone materialises nothing.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: resolved config is canonicalised into PlanId with provenance
unknown keys fail closed in authored intent
secrets never enter the evidence digest
workspace fan-out is one parent Run
path traversal is rejected, not skipped (TM.F2)
execution-capable resolution is visible in identity (TM.F1)

peerReviewRequired: Should layer 2 (user-global) affect PlanId at all? Including it makes results machine-dependent by identity; excluding it makes them machine-dependent invisibly. This artifact chose visible over portable and that is arguable.
Is an untracked local override worth supporting given it can change a verdict? The alternative is to forbid it outright.
Is the semantic universe key complete for Rust, where conditional compilation interacts with target and dependency resolution in ways this author has not verified against a real toolchain.
knownLimitations: No field-level schema for any configuration block; this fixes the resolution and identity contract, not the vocabulary.
The migrator required by the user-custody policy is referenced, not designed.

Semantic universe components for Rust are asserted from general knowledge of conditional compilation, not verified against a toolchain — the same class of unverified claim that produced two earlier errors in this exercise.
